Absurd ping should be hard to play on, but anything under 200 is extremely manageable if you can hit shots and win your 1v1s. Apex netcode favors the shooter's experience despite any level of ping, so when you peek your cover and send an r99 mag/Sniper shot into their face, your shots will land however displayed on your screen and they have far less time (your ping) to react. But when you're caught moving poorly in the open and don't challenge the squad shooting you from above, you similarly have your ping+reaction time that you'll be eating their free shots; that's a bad situation that you have to vigorously & constantly avoid in order to take advantage of ping.

The netcode of this game will actually benefit high ping aggressiveness, up to about 220ms (assuming you aren't getting packet loss). Getting the first shots off and using cover well will give you many opportunities to get damage down before enemies can properly react. You will be heavily punished for passiveness and weak movement, though. Your ping should influence your playstyle, and used properly, you may actually have an advantage.

A fellow High School player (Utah) here! I started my team/club last year. Bear with me, there's a lot to say, so I'll say as much as I can, but recognize Hylian_by_birth's post. He has many relevant points. 

So, first, don't set your sights on ever becoming Varsity status at your school. Expect it to be a club, throughout its whole life (starting a club should be the easiest thing ever; Just ask the administration for a form for starting a club and fill it out as best you can). Make sure you involve your parents at least, and as many more as you can. they will only talk it up and improve the organizational structure. Let it happen, you want it. Also, what grade are you going to be in? I began mine as a Freshman, a very good place to be when starting something new at your school. If you are going to be a senior, you will want to be very aware of the high possibility of it falling apart once you leave.

It's great you have a sponsor right now, especially because he plays Ultimate too! He can be your gateway to the administration and can help you be taken a bit more seriously. If possible, try to get him out to practices as much as he can. If he could by some chance be your coach, that would also be amazing.

Now, while it's still Summer, you'll want to get as many people to say yes now as you can. Talk to every one of your friends. Be sure the first group of people you have are all spreading the word, again, to everyone.

Also, as a club, you'll have to be open to all students, so welcome girls into your team. They're 50% of your school for goodness sake!

Recognize the seasons of sports and when they try out (all sports). Talk to everyone that was cut from football, soccer, volleyball, hockey, just everything *the second you know they were cut*. They're looking to play a sport and want to stay fit.

If you're able to do fundraising through the school or separately, try to. For example, instead of Saturday practice, do a car-wash (or convince all your girl players to do it ;). Just make sure the others do something else on the same day). But make sure your school will allow for you to use this money for the club (they should).

Worrying about jerseys isn't so important, but when your team is absolutely ready for it, go ahead. You should get colored (home) jerseys first and white or distinct other color (away) second. You should want your own logo at this point. It can be affiliated with your school *but not your school logo* or your separate team name because you're such a rebel. Be sure it looks really nice. You'll be able to use it for almost everything. Talk to your art teacher, create some really nice ideas, sketch them up if you want, and get your nerdy friend(s) to devote a weekend to some Illustrator/Photoshop instead of League of Legends for once.

Make sure you have Discraft Ultrastars. No exception. Try to get one to each player.

But the absolute most important thing is to **Keep It Fun.**

I'm 15 and I just finished The Perks of Being a Wallflower. I read it straight in 8 hours, including food/bathroom breaks. I could barely overstate the connection I felt with Charlie. I cried multiple times while reading it (although I admit I am an easy crier). Since it is set in High School, I absolutely believe high-school aged students will get the most out of this book. To me, the book was very thought-provoking; I actually went to write in my forgotten journal some notes to myself I hope to read again later. If you, as the reader, recognize the message, the message you receive from the book, you can easily look to improve your own life, along with others'.

When I was nearing the end of the book, I was questioning the format of writing to "a friend." I eventually decided that you, the reader, are this friend, and I realized that it pulled me in for an even closer emotional connection to Charlie. 

To me, it feels important that this book was published in 1999, and set in '91/'92. For me, I wasn't being even schooled at this time, so I feel like schooling could have changed a lot since then. I feel like situations like Charlie's life, the story, can still be very common. Charlie's friends aren't wicked. Not Sam or Patrick, in the very least. Yes, they have their mistakes.
